back: Wearing the enemy down by inflicting more losses of men and resources than he can replace.
A situation in which neither side can defeat the other or break through.

front: What was the aim of the Schlieffen Plan?
back: To defeat France in about six weeks through Belgium, then turn east against slowly mobilising Russia.

front: When was the Battle of Mons?
back: 23 August 1914: the BEF delayed the Germans, then retreated.

front: When was the First Battle of the Marne?
back: 6-12 September 1914: the German advance on Paris was stopped.
26-30 August 1914: Hindenburg and Ludendorff defeated a Russian army in East Prussia.

front: What was the race to the sea?
back: Autumn 1914: each side tried to outflank the other to the north until the lines reached the Channel coast.

front: Give three reasons why the Schlieffen Plan failed.
back: Belgian resistance and the BEF caused delays; Russia mobilised faster, so troops went east; exhausted German troops turned east of Paris and were hit at the Marne.

front: Why did the technology of 1914 favour defence?
back: Machine guns, rifles and artillery cut down attackers in the open, and railways brought defending reserves faster than attackers could advance.
